P1.evidence: P1a is partial — the setter was acknowledged but nothing was read back, and the rep said so explicitly: 'I had a talk with Kim. He spoke to you the other day. So he briefed me in a bit, but, you know... I'm old and kind of old-school, so I would like to hear it from you.' The prospect was told his application had been read rather than shown it. P1b is a three-part frame where the script asks for four: 'I basically want to understand, like, in depth, like, what's going on with you right now? What have you tried? And where are you actually trying to get to?' — where you are, what's in the way, where you want to go, but nothing on what you need. P1c is a miss; 'if there's an alignment, we can definitely talk about it. But if not, that's fine, too' sets a low-pressure tone but is not a frame-agreement question. P1d ran cleanly: 'walk me through, like, what's the main thing you've been looking to fix right now?'

P2.evidence: The most complete baseline in the batch. Age, height and weight all asked directly. Work covered thoroughly including the physical nature of it and the two-on-two-off roster. P2c ran properly and is usually the miss: 'Any other chronic conditions, maybe?' followed by 'Anything in the family?' P2d is a strong hit — 'Any other injuries that you remember, or anything that limits your movement?' and he then worked the club-foot disclosure hard, establishing the surgeries, the ages they happened, the physiotherapy history and a functional test, 'can you perform like a deep squat, for example, with flat feet?' Diet, sleep and energy dips all asked and answered. P2e is the one partial: gym timing was established but the rep never pinned actual days trained per week, settling for 'I don't expect myself to go to the gym every day either'.

P3.evidence: Genuinely excellent and the best goals work in the batch. P3a ran twice, including the ideal-body-type question. P3c is a clean hit via bouldering: 'A lot of my mates boulder, but I doubt I could even get up, you know, the first, the most beginner rock, so I won't even try it.' P3d is textbook: 'why is that important to you?' P3e ran as 'what would that moment be worth to you?' P3g is where this call earns its score — the rep drove all the way through to identity and got the insight, 'the issue wasn't really you not trying hard. The issue was with the confidence and the standards that you held yourself to... because that was your identity.' P3h reflected back accurately and got agreement: 'the biggest goal underneath that is you becoming healthy for the future version of you... Does that feel accurate?' P3f is scored a miss under the volunteered-information rule — the fiancée and future children came from the prospect unprompted and the rep echoed them back ('you probably want to have kids, too') rather than ever asking who else this impacts.

P4.evidence: Complete. P4a and P4b via the loss-and-regain history. P4c ran verbatim in substance: 'what do you feel has actually been stopping you from fixing this up to this point?' P4d and P4e both landed with the prospect naming it himself — 'I think drinking's probably one of my bigger problems and lack of accountability.' P4f is a hit in a stronger form than the script asks for: rather than 'the information isn't the problem', the rep reframed the mechanism — 'This partying cycle is putting the blame on something external... there's some, there was something underneath that, that you were trying to cover with partying' — and got a genuinely deep answer about deriving self-worth from buying friends drinks.

P5.evidence: The phase ran but never bit. P5a is near-verbatim: 'what would your life look like one year from now, two years from now, if you'd actually just stay like you are right now?' P5b ran twice, 'is staying at this current level acceptable to you?' and 'How does that actually sit with you?' Both times the answer came back soft — 'I think there's always room for improvement', 'I'm pretty happy with what I've progressed' — and P5c is partial because the rep did not press the why-not against those answers. P5d is partial: 'can I keep you accountable to everything that you shared with me, that the highest standards that you want to be living up to?' is a commitment-to-accountability question rather than a line in the sand, and it got a conditional yes. The cost of inaction was never made real, which is why the price landed with nothing pulling against it.

P6.evidence: The cleanest P6 in the batch and the one place the rep applied his manager's certainty-language coaching from the previous day. P6a: 'Do you agree, like, you would finally get where you want to be, to be the confident Fletcher proud of themselves?' — 'A hundred percent.' P6b: 'If we can figure out the details, are you fully committed to showing up for yourself and doing the work...' The prospect hedged with 'I think so', and the rep caught it and pushed back — 'You think so?' — until he got 'I am. It's about, I need to commit, and there's no better time than now.' P6c is satisfied: he had a clear yes before presenting price.

P11.evidence: A close was attempted at three separate price points so the phase applies. Nothing in it ran. No payment collected and no link sent at any tier including the $199 community. No Trevor onboarding scheduled. No agreement email, no signature. No welcome email, no Skool link sent, no onboarding questionnaire — notable because the rep screen-shared the Skool community as a downsell and still did not send the join link when the prospect said he was leaning toward it.

objection_plays.detail: The front half ran well and the back half did not run at all. Isolate landed first and correctly: 'Like, finances aside, let's put that for a pause for a second... do you genuinely believe that this can actually get you to the goal that we just covered?' and then 'Is anything else that's keeping you from being 100% in?' The should-versus-how move ran near-verbatim: 'So you're not in a, should I do it, place. It's more of a, how can I actually do it, financially, to get to your goals?' Permission for the money conversation was asked and granted: 'would you be open to actually discuss finances... and how we can actually maybe navigate around that to make it more digestible to you?' Then the play stopped. Of the six financial-picture moves, one was attempted — 'You don't have the full amount or you have some of that?' — and the rep accepted a non-answer and never returned. Monthly surplus, number of credit cards, available credit per card, used versus available, and crypto or stocks were all skipped entirely. Instead of opening the wallet he cut the price, which is the opposite move. The payment-plan line was also inverted: the script says 'most clients pay upfront, but for some we break it up', the rep said 'we don't have any set payment plans in place, like, it's all customized' and then structured nothing.

Triggered by 'a big amount like that will not go down well with the misses.' The rep spotted the contradiction with what the prospect had said earlier and challenged it — 'Why? I thought you said that she's supportive' — then asked the best question available, which is not in the script: 'Is she aware of everything that we actually went through today, like in depth?' He built on the answer once ('So she doesn't know that if it was possible for you to do it by yourself, you've already been there') and then dropped the thread when the prospect asked to end the call. None of the remaining scripted moves ran: no 'what obstacles might come up when you talk to her', no 'is there any reason she would NOT want you stronger', no 'is this her input or permission to bet on yourself', no deposit-with-refund fallback. The last of these was the obvious play here and would have cost nothing.

Triggered by 'it's something I'm not going to decide tonight, and it's something I do need to sleep upon.' Two moves ran. The when-do-you-decide-differently move: 'there's always putting it off like tomorrow i'm gonna go to the gym tomorrow i'm gonna start eating clean like there's no tomorrow it's only today man.' And a risk-minimisation variant applied to the downsell: 'you can commit today and you can quit tomorrow that's it 200 that's that's what you're risking.' The core diagnostic move — 'so what's actually coming up that's preventing you from getting started?' — was never asked in this sequence, which matters because the answer was already on the table and was simply that he had no money. The 'that man you want to be, how does HE decide right now' move was gestured at but not run.

Triggered repeatedly by fatigue and readiness rather than by season — 'maybe I'm not ready to commit', 'I need to go to bed', 'I'm not going to spend my first day on it going straight to bed I'll start it tomorrow if anything.' The rep ran the only-right-now move ('The only thing you can control is right now' in the form of 'there's no tomorrow it's only today man'). No other OD move ran. Scoring this as adherence is uncomfortable and should be read alongside the conduct flag: the OD play assumes the objection is a stalling frame, and here it was a man with a twelve-hour underground shift starting in under eight hours.

No fear or doubt objection arose after price. The rep did run a strong proactive OE-style resistance pre-frame before presenting — 'with anything in life, especially when it comes to change, there's almost always some level of resistance... probably in the moment, like, even before this call ends, you may feel some level of resistance' — followed by the devil-and-angel exercise. That is good practice and is credited in P5/P3, not here.

SCRIPT GAP — no play exists for a prospect who genuinely cannot pay, as distinct from one who will not. OC is built to distinguish should-I from how-can-I and then find the money; it has no branch for a verified negative answer. Here the prospect did the arithmetic out loud in three currencies ('$6,000 for six months is $1,000 a month. 250 USD per week, and AUD, that's 400') and concluded 'in my current financial state, it is impossible.' With no scripted exit, the rep improvised downward twice, which is how a $6,000 offer became $199 a month inside twenty minutes.

SCRIPT GAP — no play exists for a prospect who arrives with no price expectation whatsoever. 'I was under the impression that I was just going to be like free for some reason' is a qualification failure upstream of the closer, and the script gives him nothing to do with it except the rhetorical 'Does your PT also work for free?' There is no move for resetting an anchor of zero, and no defined handoff back to the setter.

notes: Phases 2 through 4 and phase 6 are the best work in this batch and should be used as a coaching example — particularly the P4f reframe that got a genuine identity insight, and the P6b moment where he refused to accept 'I think so'. Two coaching points. First, P5 ran but never bit: he asked the right questions, accepted soft answers, and never pressed 'why not', so there was no cost of inaction holding the frame when price landed. Second and more important, when the money objection came he abandoned the play at exactly the point it starts working — he isolated, got permission for the financial conversation, and then took none of the financial picture and cut the price instead. The largest issue on this call is not adherence at all: it is that a prospect this far outside the ICP and this far from being able to pay reached a 76-minute closer call in the first place.
